title: NHL Jersey Quiz Part 2: Hard Mode
headline: NHL Jersey Quiz Part 2: Name The Team From A Tiny Piece Of Its Jersey
description: A hard NHL jersey quiz: eight tiny squares cut from current NHL home sweaters, no numbers, no crests, no shoulder patches. Just a sleeve stripe or a hem. Guess the team, reveal the answer, keep score.
intro: Every piece below is a small square cut from a current NHL home sweater, about one fiftieth of the whole picture. No numbers, no crests, no shoulder patches. What is left is the stuff fans stop noticing: the stripes on a sleeve, the bands at the hem.
Make your guess, then tap Show The Answer. Be honest and mark whether you got it, and your score adds up at the bottom.

items.hint: Hard mode. No numbers, no crests.
items.piece: Gold stripes with white piping on the sleeve of the royal blue home sweater.
items.fact: Buffalo went back to royal blue in 2020. The home sweater has three gold stripes with white piping on each sleeve and at the hem.

items.piece: The silver line where the burgundy body meets the blue hem of the home sweater.
items.fact: The Avalanche moved from Quebec in 1995 and won the Stanley Cup in their first season in Denver.

items.piece: Blue and white stripes above an orange band on the sleeve of the blue home sweater.
items.fact: Edmonton's blue home sweater has orange shoulders and orange and white stripes on the sleeves and the hem.

items.piece: Where the orange body meets the white sleeve and its black cuff on the orange home sweater.
items.fact: Co-founder Bill Putnam picked orange, black and white in 1966, before the team had a name, because he wanted hot colors.

items.piece: A thin white line where the gold body meets the navy hem of the gold home sweater.
items.fact: Nashville made gold its home color in 2011. Before that, the Predators wore navy at home.

items.piece: Silver and white bands at the hem of the black home sweater.
items.fact: The Kings switched from purple and gold to black and silver in 1988, the year Wayne Gretzky arrived from Edmonton.

items.piece: Black and white stripes at the hem of the teal home sweater.
items.fact: The Sharks have worn Pacific teal since their first season, 1991-92.

items.piece: A wide red stripe across the sleeve of the black home sweater.
items.fact: The franchise moved from Hartford, where it was the Whalers, to North Carolina in 1997, and won the Stanley Cup in 2006.
